lead: People in India have studied the sky for about 3,000 years: first with their eyes and maths, then with giant stone instruments, and now with radio dishes and spacecraft. This page puts all of it on one map.
try: Press Play 3,000 years and watch the map of India light up. Then tap any dot to read its story.
points: About 1,500 years ago, Aryabhata worked out that the Earth spins, and measured one turn to within a hundredth of a second, with no telescope.
Indian ways of counting, including zero, travelled to Baghdad and from there around the world.
The same curiosity runs from old books to today's missions: India now has its own telescopes on mountains and spacecraft at the Moon, Mars and the Sun.
